 1   Christ in Brooklyn.

 2                Reverend Gardner Taylor was the 

 3   grandson of slaves who took over the Concord 

 4   Baptist Church pulpit in Brooklyn in 1948.  He 

 5   became an influential voice for civil rights and 

 6   one of the nation's most eloquent churchmen in 

 7   this country.  His impact as a speaker, a writer, 

 8   a political force in the City and in the nation 

 9   of long-segregated schools, churches and other 

10   institutions reached far beyond his 10,000-member 

11   congregation.  

12                He was the author of many books and 

13   2,000 sermons and the recipient of 15 honorary 

14   doctorates.  In 1980, Time magazine called him 

15   the dean of black preachers in America.  In 1966, 

16   Baylor University in Louisiana said he was one of 

17   the most effective preachers in the 

18   English-speaking world.

19                "At a time when white society" -- 

20   and this is a quote from Dr. Taylor, "at a time 

21   when society, by statute, custom and 

22   conversation, just called us 'niggers.' ...  How 

23   could we have survived without a sense of God and 

24   the church telling us that we do matter?"

25                Dr. Taylor delivered lectures in 


                                                                4170

 1   Scotland, England, Australia, China, Japan, South 

 2   Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and at universities and 

 3   churches across the United States.

 4                He gave the pre-inauguration sermon 

 5   for President Elect Bill Clinton at the 

 6   Metropolitan A.M.E. Church in Washington, D.C., 

 7   and in 2000 he received the Presidential Medal of 

 8   Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, 

 9   from President Clinton.  

10                In New York Dr. Taylor organized 

11   civil rights marches and was arrested three times 

12   during protests in the 1960s.  He was director of 

13   the Urban League of Greater New York, a member of 

14   the New York City Commission on Intergroup 

15   Relations, and a leader of the Kings County 

16   Democratic Organization.  

17                In 1958, Mayor Robert F. Wagner, 

18   Jr., named him to the New York City Board of 

19   Education as the second black member in the 

20   board's history.

21                In 1988 Dr. Taylor, before leaving 

22   his congregation in retirement, raised $1 million 

23   to establish the Christ Fund, a church endowment 

24   whose annual interest is used to provide 

25   community improvement grants to Central Brooklyn 


                                                                4171

 1   neighborhoods, so far totaling more than the 

 2   $1 million original endowment.

 4   the Interdenominational Theological Center in 

 5   Atlanta, Georgia.  His books include How Shall 

 6   They Preach, The Scarlet Thread, Chariots of 

 7   Flame, We Have This Ministry, and Faith in the 

 8   Fire: Wisdom for Life.

10   Church of Christ, as well as members of the 

11   Brooklyn community at large and the nation of 

12   ministers across the country, mourn the passing 

13   of Dr. Gardner C. Taylor and shall never forget 

14   how much he meant to people in this nation and in 

15   his own church and community.

21   Gardner C. Taylor.
